react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis) converged on sulfur amino-acid metabolism as the dominant biological signal. In RaMP ORA, KEGG:map00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) ranked first with FDR = 3.86 × 10⁻¹⁴ and fold-enrichment = 711, driven by six input metabolites (L-methionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cysteine, (R)-lipoic acid, L-ornithine, 2-oxobutanoate). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked KEGG:hsa00270 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism) at rank 1 with p = 0.0002, with four hits (L-methionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cysteine, 2-oxobutanoate). Mummichog's m/z-direct network confirmed the same cluster at ranks 1–4, with Glycine/serine/alanine/threonine metabolism (p = 0.0050) and Methionine/cysteine metabolism (p = 0.033) as the top network neighbourhoods. A secondary cluster centred on the urea cycle (L-ornithine + 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid, p = 0.0050) and tyrosine metabolism (5,6-dihydroxyindole + phenylephrine, p = 0.0083) emerged in mummichog and was independently supported by MetaboAnalystR (Arginine/proline metabolism, p = 0.0396). The driver metabolites — L-methionine, S-adenosylhomocysteine, L-cysteine, and 2-oxobutanoate — form a metabolic module linked through the methionine cycle and trans-sulfuration pathway, where S-adenosylhomocysteine is the product of methyltransferase reactions and L-cysteine is the trans-sulfuration product of homocysteine. The coordinated perturbation of these metabolites in the treatment group is consistent with altered methyl-donor availability and/or oxidative-stress response capacity.
